metaTitle: Best Snow Blowers for Sidewalks, Compared (2026)
metaDescription: Six narrow, light snow blowers and shovels compared for sidewalks and walkways, corded and cordless, with width, throw and chute control explained.
expertTake: A sidewalk wants a narrow, light, easy-to-aim machine, and the SENIX 18-inch is the best balance of path and handling. The 21V 14-inch shovel is the best light tool for narrow walks, and the corded STEELITE is the pick if an outlet is close. Skip a wide machine on a sidewalk, because you will fight the width more than you gain. Measure the walk and check local rules before you buy. A spare battery or a short cord makes a long walk easier.
introParagraphs: Sidewalks and walkways are narrow, long and often bordered by a lawn, a hedge or a street. A machine that suits them has to be light enough to steer, narrow enough to fit and able to throw cleared snow to one side instead of back onto the walk. The right tool is the one that leaves the snow where you want it.

Width is the first number to check, because a path wider than the walk forces you to throw snow into a neighbour's yard or the road. The chute then matters as much as the motor, since where the snow lands decides whether you finish the job or do it twice. Measure the walk first, then pick a tool. A short trial pass tells you more than any spec.

products.name: SENIX 40V 18-inch cordless blower, 2 x 4Ah
products.description:
The SENIX 18-inch is the best balance for a long sidewalk. An 18-inch path fits most residential walks with room to spare, and a 180-degree chute lets you aim snow onto the lawn side. The 1,500 watt brushless motor and steel auger handle typical snowfall.

Its 33-foot throw is long enough to clear a berm at the curb, and two 4Ah batteries are rated for about a 10-car driveway in 8 inches of snow, which is a lot of sidewalk. A built-in LED light bar helps on dark mornings.

Against the shovels it rolls on wheels, so you do not carry the weight. Against the 21-inch machines it is easier to steer on a narrow walk. If the walk runs alongside a street, aim the chute toward the lawn and check local rules before throwing into the road. Keep a spare set of packs charged for a very long walk. It is also the model to pick if you want to avoid carrying weight on a long walk.
products.bestFor: Long sidewalks that need a light wheeled machine with good aim.
pros: 180-degree chute aims snow onto the lawn
Wheeled so you do not carry the weight
cons: Two 4Ah packs limit a very long walk

products.name: EGO Power+ SNT2122 21-inch single-stage, 2 x 4Ah
products.description:
The SNT2122 is wider than most sidewalk tools at 21 inches, but variable auger speed and a 180-degree chute make it controllable. Two 4Ah packs are rated for about a 10-car driveway in 8 inches of snow.

On a narrow walk it is a bit large, so use it for walks that are at least four feet wide. Its 42-foot throw clears a long way from the walk, which helps if the plow berm sits at the curb.

It shares packs with EGO tools. Store the packs indoors and keep it on paved surfaces. If your walk is narrow, test the width against the paving before ordering, since a 21-inch path leaves little margin. It is best on a wide walk that leads into a driveway. On a wide walk it will save time, but on a narrow one it will feel clumsy.
products.bestFor: Wide sidewalks and walks that run into a drive.
cons: 21 inches is wide for a narrow walk

products.name: 21V 14-inch cordless snow shovel, 830W, two batteries
products.description:
This 14-inch shovel comes with two batteries and a charger, which the listing says gives over 50 minutes of runtime. An adjustable deflector sends snow to the front, 45 degrees left or 45 degrees right, so you can aim it onto the lawn side of a walk.

A 830 watt all-copper motor runs at up to 16,000 RPM, and an LED display shows the charge. Against a wheeled blower it is lighter and cheaper but you carry the weight and cover less ground per minute.

It is a good match for a narrow walk and a couple of steps. Check the box contents and the battery rating before you buy. Because the listing is a generic-brand tool, check warranty and battery availability before you buy, and note the charge level on the display before each use. It works well for a short walk plus a couple of steps.
products.bestFor: Narrow walks and steps where a light shovel is enough.
pros: Two batteries included with a stated 50 minutes of runtime
Deflector aims snow left, right or front
Light and cheap compared with a blower

products.name: STEELITE 20-inch corded electric blower, 15A brushless
products.description:
The STEELITE corded blower has a 15 amp brushless motor, a 20-inch path and a 10-inch snow intake depth. It is rated for up to 860 pounds per minute and has dual LED lights and an adjustable chute.

The listing stresses that it is corded and needs a power cord, so it suits a sidewalk close to an outlet. A long walk is awkward because the cord reaches only so far and creates a trip hazard.

It is a good unit for a short walk beside the house. On a long walk, the cord is the main limit, so plan the route to work away from the outlet and keep the cord on the cleared side. It is a quiet, simple way to clear a short walk.
products.bestFor: Short walks close to an outlet.

products.name: VOLTASK 24V 13.2-inch cordless snow shovel, 4Ah, 23 ft throw
products.description:
The VOLTASK shovel clears a path of about 13 inches and throws up to 23 feet from a 24V 4Ah battery with about 30 minutes of continuous runtime. An ergonomic handle reduces strain.

It is a light tool for narrow walks and steps, and 23 feet of throw clears snow from a typical walk onto the lawn. Against the 21V shovel with two batteries it has a single pack but a more established listing.

Use it for light snow and short sessions. It is a good second tool for steps even if you own a bigger machine for the drive. Its single battery means it is best for short sessions.
products.bestFor: Short walks and steps with light snow.

products.name: Westinghouse WSnow20 20-inch corded blower, steel auger
products.description:
The WSnow20 is a corded 20-inch machine with a steel auger and a 25-foot throw. It has a rotating chute and dual LED lights.

Its limit on a sidewalk is the cord, which restricts how far you can go from an outlet. On a short walk near the house it is the lowest-maintenance option.

Use a heavy outdoor cord. Pair it with a heavy outdoor cord and plan the route so the cord stays on the cleared side. It is the cheapest route to a steel-auger blower for a short walk. Use a heavy-gauge extension cord.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Sidewalks are typically three to five feet wide, so a 14 to 20-inch path is plenty. A machine wider than the walk forces awkward turns. The 14-inch shovels and 18-inch SENIX fit; the 21-inch EGO suits wider walks. Measure your actual sidewalk before choosing, because a path that is a few inches wider than the walk is wasted and makes the machine harder to steer between a lawn edge and a hedge. Always test a small section first to see where the snow lands.

Where the snow lands matters on a narrow walk. A 180-degree chute, as on the SENIX and EGO, lets you aim onto the lawn. The 21V shovel's deflector offers front, left and right settings. Think about where the snow will land before you start. Throwing onto the lawn is the best case; throwing into the road may be against local rules and can bury a parked car. Check whether the walk has a slope, because a heavy machine is hard to hold back on a descent.

Shovels like the 21V and VOLTASK are light but you carry them. Wheeled blowers like the SENIX roll, which helps on a long walk. Shovels are light but tiring after twenty minutes, while a wheeled machine takes the weight. Pick by the length of the walk, not by the price. Wet snow is heavier, so a shovel will tire you faster than usual.

The EGO throws about 42 feet, the SENIX 33 and the VOLTASK 23. Longer throw puts snow past the walk and the berm. A longer throw is useful where the lawn is deep or there is a berm at the curb. It also means you do not have to clear the same snow twice. Wind changes the best throw direction, so a chute with a wide range helps.

A long sidewalk is hard to clear with a cord. Cordless machines roam freely. Corded machines suit walks near an outlet. A cord is a poor match for a long sidewalk, since you will run out of reach or have to move the outlet end repeatedly. Cordless is the better choice for anything beyond about fifty feet. Keep the cord short and well clear of the path you have yet to clear.

A long walk can drain a single battery. The 21V shovel includes two batteries; the SENIX includes two 4Ah packs. Count the minutes of runtime against the minutes the walk takes by hand. A single battery is usually enough for a short walk but not a long one. A spare battery makes the difference on a long walk.

faq.q: What size is best for a sidewalk?
faq.a: A path of 14 to 20 inches is plenty for a typical walk. A narrow machine is easier to steer and fits most walks. Check the width of your walk with a tape measure before you buy.

faq.q: Shovel or blower for a sidewalk?
faq.a: A shovel suits steps and short walks. A wheeled blower suits a long walk. A shovel is also easier to carry up a flight of steps.

faq.q: Can I throw snow onto the lawn?
faq.a: Yes, with a chute or deflector that aims to the side. Aim the chute before you start and again when you turn. Test the aim on a small patch first.
Cordless roams freely. Corded suits walks near an outlet. A cord is fine near the house but awkward on a long walk.

faq.a: Rules vary by town. Check your local rules before throwing into the road. Check your town rules before throwing snow into the road. If in doubt, throw onto your own lawn.
